codeReview.summary: The migration correctly renames runner.js to runner.ts, preserves runtime behavior, and includes the requested ESLint globalIgnores for compiled lib/**/*.js and lib/**/*.js.map. However, one required behavior is not fully met: runner event constants are not actually typed as string literals in a way TypeScript can enforce.

issues.description: Feature expectation 'All event constants typed as string literals' is not satisfied. `constants` is created via `utils.defineConstants(...)`, whose current signature returns `Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>` (lib/utils.ts:555-557), so literal event values are widened/erased. This is visible in downstream casts like `this.state = constants.STATE_IDLE as string` (lib/runner.ts:294, 1269, 1287), indicating the event/state constants are not strongly typed literal unions.

sharedStateObservations.observation: The migration guidance says to type EventEmitter event names as string literals, but shared utility typing currently erases literal types when using `utils.defineConstants`, making this requirement easy to miss.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: migration-worker SKILL.md (Type Quality + EventEmitter guidance) vs lib/utils.ts:555-557 (`defineConstants(obj: Record<string, unknown>): Readonly<Record<string, unknown>>`) and lib/runner.ts casts (`as string`) at lines 294/1269/1287.

summary: Reviewed core-runner (commit 4f26af7ceab562528b03c2a1ea83e3c2ba8ee92b): migration and ESLint ignore fix are largely correct, but the required string-literal typing for Runner constants is not actually enforced by current types, so this review is marked fail with one blocking issue.
